PASS WITH NOTES -- round 2, delta ad27621c0f995aaf4cafcd9937257ebc84018c09 -> c8d2eab2fc9e073d8c8b8de27dbb53e8141ec315.

R280-001/P280-001 is fixed: attach contention performs one nonblocking lock attempt and returns `Busy`, rather than sleeping on a runtime worker or forking the read. The cross-process attach/setup guard remains in place. No new error-to-absence path was found that grants deletion, revival or false observed-dead tombstones. The consumer trace below is the evidence that UNKNOWN is a brake, not fabricated pane absence. One newly identified downstream retry gap is recorded as a C34 follow-up, not an unsolicited third-round gate.

## C34 follow-up F232: Codex binder consumes a transient error without retry

First surfaced during this round's requested downstream trace (also identified independently by performance): `CodexBinder::bind_once` (`codex_bind.rs:242-257`) updates `seen.locks` and `seen.rows` before probing. `bind_seat:301` propagates the pane-query error, but `bind_once:261-265` merely logs it and returns success. On subsequent ticks, unchanged pending rows and thread-lock sets are filtered out at `253`. The resilient binder wrapper (`crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:797-815`) keeps ticking but does not reset Seen.

Thus a one-shot Busy error after otherwise-valid Codex child/thread evidence can leave that spawned row unbound until another Codex thread appears, the row changes, or the daemon restarts. This caching behavior predates the PR, but Busy adds a normal transient producer for it. It is NOT an error-to-pane-absence or tombstone path. No ordinary alternate automatic retry was found in the binder wrapper. Proposed scoped repair: retain retry eligibility for actual probe errors, with the existing bounded cadence/cost discipline; do not turn every genuinely unbindable row into a per-tick process census.

An isolated deterministic one-shot pane-query-error probe reproduced this: the first bind returned zero, 30 unchanged ticks made zero further probe attempts and left the seat unbound, then adding an unrelated thread lock triggered a successful bind of the same valid seat. This injects the consumer error directly, not a real Codex/Tmux timing canary. pm-001 explicitly ruled this F232, a FOLLOW-UP, not a round-two block (message `4312afcf872ab5a5-00000000000000f3`): it requires overlapping Codex spawn and another process's attach, recovers on a new row/thread or restart, touches no absence/tombstone decision, and must not hold up the whole-server crash fix. Silkworm owns the separate small PR. The scoped repair is to avoid consuming seen-row/lock eligibility when the pane probe errors.

Spawn's early failed-unbound answer is not a second finding: `http/mod.rs:1993-2037` and `spawn_waits.rs:163-199` intentionally preserve later binding and parent handoff (F211), along with the dispatched seat/pane. It is not a claim of absence or death.

## Lock and cost contract

`control.rs:391-396` still acquires the owning guard before launching and holds it until setup's sentinel answers. It is local to start, never retained by Live. Contended acquisition (`490-513`) contains no sleep, polling loop, thread join or blocking flock; it tries `File::try_lock` once. A distinct `AttachLockHeld` error type (`520-541`) prevents spawn EAGAIN being misclassified as contention.

The new code removes the acquisition-wait source of R280-001. It does NOT make every old tmux operation asynchronous: the pre-existing successful-start handshake, reply wait, file operations and state mutex remain synchronous. No stronger claim is made.

Cost needs the requested five-second boundary:

- During the initial contention window, reads are skipped: zero tmux launches, no retry timer/loop. Each eligible control-query attempt opens the lock file and calls try_lock once; the next caller/read cadence supplies the next attempt.
- A public `pane_process` call can make two eligible queries because of its existing failed-read disambiguating list. Thus "one try_lock per read" means per control-query attempt, not necessarily per public port call.
- The observer's first global list fails during Busy, so it stops that pass before its per-pane reads: approximately 1.67 lock attempts/s at the unchanged 600 ms cadence, not a new 100 Hz poll per pane.
- At five seconds of observed contention, `ask:336-346` deliberately returns Fork and stamps the old five-second failed-start backoff. During that backoff, each fallback-enabled read still forks. Under a permanently held lock, demand alternates Busy windows and fork-backoff windows; zero launches is NOT an unconditional denial-cost guarantee.
- In a fork window, the nominal observer demand remains `(1+3N)/0.6` tmux launches/s per affected daemon (401.7/s for 80 tracked panes), plus request-driven reads. Serial launch cost and skipped/stalled passes reduce achieved average rates. There is no workload-independent fork-rate ceiling. No launches occur for live-only unavailable reads.

Under C33 a same-user held lock remains accepted. The lock is a BRAKE: removing it permits more attaches; unknown reads only spare/defer. S280-001 (creation follows umask rather than enforcing a private mode) stays the explicitly recorded C34 follow-up; it is not reopened as a round-two blocker. Filename sanitization and dot-file sweep exclusion are unchanged. No deployment or live-fleet contention was injected.
